mainTopic: Why פסוקים are needed for ולד חטאת and תמורת אשם despite a הלכה, what ״אָשָׁם הוּא״ teaches according to רב, and a challenge to רבי יוחנן's rule about a נזיר.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: the פסוק teaches that offspring of קדשים such as שלמים are offered, not left to die. Next, a ברייתא uses the word ״רַק״ to teach that ולד חטאת and תמורת אשם are not offered on the מזבח. The גמרא asks why a פסוק is needed when a הלכה למשה מסיני already covers both cases. It answers that the הלכה tells us what to do with the animal, and the פסוק adds that someone who offers it anyway breaks an עשה. Then רבי עקיבא learns the rule from ״אָשָׁם הוּא״, and the גמרא asks the same question about his source. The answer is that ״הוּא״ teaches the rule behind רב's ruling: an אשם that was sent to graze is valid if slaughtered as an עולה, but before that it is not valid. Finally, the גמרא goes back to רבי יוחנן's statement that a certain rule is a הלכה about a נזיר. It starts to challenge him with a ברייתא about others who bring pairs of birds, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The verse teaches that offspring of sacred animals are not left to die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier explanation. Without the פסוק we might have thought offspring of other קדשים are brought to the בית הבחירה and left to die there, so the פסוק teaches that they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Without the verse, I might have thought the offspring of sacred animals are brought to the Temple and left there to die. The verse teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from just before: it explains what mistake the פסוק stops us from making about the offspring of קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might have thought every offspring of a קרבן is simply brought to the מקדש and left to die. The words ״קא משמע לן דלא״ reject that idea. Offspring of קדשים such as שלמים are not left to die; they are offered.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring born to animals set aside as קרבנות
The 'chosen house', meaning the בית המקדש
'It teaches us', showing what new point the source makes

phrases.english: and the offspring of sacred animals [are left to die] in the Temple,
it teaches us that [it is] not [so].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an explanation that began before this section, about why the פסוק is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the mistake the פסוק prevents
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Offspring of קדשים are brought to the מקדש and left to die.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are not left to die; they are offered.

steps.title: The ברייתא: ולד חטאת and תמורת אשם are excluded by the word ״רַק״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. We might have thought ולד חטאת and תמורת אשם are also offered, so the פסוק says ״רַק״ to exclude them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא teaches: You might have thought the offspring of a sin-offering and the substitute of a guilt-offering are also treated this way. So the verse says, 'Only.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next part of the ברייתא, which uses the word ״רַק״ to exclude two kinds of animals from being offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary offspring of קדשים are offered, but the ברייתא says ולד חטאת and תמורת אשם are different. The small word ״רַק״ ('only') is read as a limiting word that leaves them out. This sets up the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It teaches', used to quote the ברייתא
The offspring of an animal set aside as a חטאת
An animal someone tried to swap in for an אשם; it becomes holy too
'The verse teaches', introducing the source
'Only', a limiting word that excludes something

phrases.english: It teaches: One might think that even the offspring of a sin-offering
and the substitute of a guilt-offering [are treated] so —
phrases.notes: 'So' means offered on the מזבח, like the original קרבן.

phrases.english: the verse states: 'Only.'

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי: יָכוֹל אַף וְלַד חַטָּאת וּתְמוּרַת אָשָׁם כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא with a new exclusion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of ״רַק״, ולד חטאת and תמורת אשם are not offered like the original קרבנות.

steps.title: Why a verse, if a tradition already teaches that ולד חטאת dies?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. There is a הלכה למשה מסיני that ולד חטאת is left to die, so why would a פסוק be needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a verse? We know it by tradition: the offspring of a sin-offering goes to its death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's use of ״רַק״: the law about ולד חטאת is already known from a הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes the תורה does not use a פסוק to teach something we already know. The tradition already says ולד חטאת is left to die. So the ״רַק״ seems to be teaching nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why do I need a verse?', asking why a פסוק seems unnecessary
'It is learned as a הלכה', a tradition from משה at סיני
'Goes to death', meaning it is locked away until it dies

steps.confusionAlert: 'Left to die' does not mean someone kills the animal. It is kept away and not fed until it dies on its own.

phrases.english: Why do I need a verse?
It is learned as a tradition:
the offspring of a sin-offering goes to death!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי קְרָא? הִילְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of ״רַק״ to exclude ולד חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק should not be needed for a law already known from a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: Answer: the verse comes for the guilt-offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that ולד חטאת is known from the הלכה. It says the פסוק is really needed for תמורת אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is indeed so; the verse comes for the guilt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge about ולד חטאת and moves the פסוק's purpose to אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא mentioned two cases, and the הלכה covers only the first one. So the גמרא says ״רַק״ is needed for the second case, תמורת אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That is indeed so', agreeing with the questioner
'The verse came for the אשם'

phrases.english: That is indeed so,
and the verse came for the guilt-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי, וּקְרָא לְאָשָׁם הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by limiting the פסוק to אשם.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agrees in part and moves the פסוק to the other case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק of ״רַק״ is extra, since the חטאת law is already known.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is needed for תמורת אשם.

steps.title: But the guilt-offering also has a tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. There is also a הלכה for אשם: whatever would be left to die with a חטאת is left to graze with an אשם. So the פסוק still seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: The guilt-offering is also learned by tradition: anything that with a sin-offering would be left to die, with a guilt-offering is left to graze!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 4 by showing that אשם also has a known הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule: any case where a חטאת would be left to die is a case where an אשם is sent to graze. Since a תמורת חטאת dies, a תמורת אשם grazes, and we already know this. So once again the פסוק seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Anything that with a חטאת would die'
'With an אשם, it grazes' until it gets a מום

phrases.english: The guilt-offering too is learned as a tradition:
anything that, if it were with a sin-offering, would die,
with a guilt-offering, grazes!
phrases.notes: It is left in the field until it gets a blemish, so it can no longer go on the מזבח.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פסוק is needed for אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A הלכה already covers אשם too, so the פסוק is still extra.

steps.title: The verse adds a positive commandment for someone who offers it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא's final answer: from the הלכה alone we would know what to do, but not that offering the animal is a sin. The פסוק teaches that offering it breaks an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: if we had only the tradition, I would say: that is the law, but if he offered it anyway, he would not be liable for anything at all. The verse teaches that if he offers it, he transgresses a positive commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer: the פסוק adds a penalty level, an עשה, that the הלכה alone would not give.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה tells us how to handle the animal: let the ולד חטאת die and send the תמורת אשם to graze. It does not say that offering it is a sin. The פסוק ״רַק... תשא ובאת״ adds that offering such an animal breaks an עשה, so the פסוק is not extra after all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather', dropping the earlier answer for a new one
'I would have said', the mistaken first thought
'He offered it' on the מזבח
'He would not be liable for anything'
'He stands in violation of an עשה', a positive commandment

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה למשה מסיני tells us what to do with ולד חטאת and תמורת אשם. The פסוק ״רַק״ adds that someone who offers them on the מזבח breaks an עשה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a הלכה and a פסוק can teach the same rule, and the פסוק is still needed because it adds a level of איסור.

phrases.english: Rather: if [we knew it only] from the tradition,
I would have said: [that is] the law,
but if he offered it —
he would not be liable for it, not anything at all,
the verse teaches us
that if he offers it —
he transgresses a positive commandment through it.
phrases.notes: The עשה comes from the same פסוק, ״רַק... תשא ובאת״ (דברים 12:26).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after step 5 rejected step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק adds a level of איסור beyond the הלכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the הלכה, someone who offered the animal would not be liable at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Offering ולד חטאת or תמורת אשם breaks an עשה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה sets what to do with the animal, and the פסוק makes offering it an עשה violation.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's source: the word 'It is'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says no special derivation is needed, because the פסוק ״אָשָׁם הוּא״ already shows that only the original אשם is offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: You don't need that. The פסוק says "It is a guilt-offering." That means it stays as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא. Now it gives רבי עקיבא's opinion about where we learn that a תמורת אשם is not offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the ברייתא learned the rule from the word ״רַק״. רבי עקיבא says there is a simpler source: the word ״הוּא״ ("it") in the פסוק about אשם. ״הוּא״ means only this exact animal, in its present form, is the אשם, not an animal swapped for it.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is a guilt-offering" — the words in the פסוק that רבי עקיבא learns from
"It shall be in its state" — only the animal as it is now
An animal someone tried to swap in place of a קרבן; it becomes holy too

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: it is not necessary,
for it says: "It is a guilt-offering"
— it shall be in its present state.
phrases.notes: He means only the real אשם itself is offered, not an animal swapped for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי עקיבא's other source for the rule about תמורת אשם, in place of ״רַק״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word ״הוּא״ in ״אָשָׁם הוּא״ teaches that only the original אשם is offered.

steps.title: Why need a verse if there is a tradition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא needs a פסוק at all, since the הלכה already says whatever dies with a חטאת is left to graze with an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a פסוק? We have it as a tradition: whatever would be left to die with a חטאת is left to graze with an אשם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's derivation. It says the rule is already known from a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as in Step 5, now aimed at רבי עקיבא. A תמורת חטאת is left to die, so by the tradition a תמורת אשם is left to graze. That already shows it cannot be offered, so the word ״הוּא״ seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: "We learned it as a tradition" — a rule handed down from משה, not taken from a פסוק
Is left to die (said about a חטאת that cannot be offered)
Grazes — it is left to graze until it gets a blemish, then it is sold

phrases.english: Why do I need a verse?
We learned it as a tradition:
whatever is left to die in the case of a sin-offering
— is left to graze in the case of a guilt-offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי עקיבא's derivation in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's use of ״אָשָׁם הוּא״ to exclude a תמורת אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק should not be needed for something already known from a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: The verse teaches רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees the הלכה covers the תמורת אשם. It says the פסוק is needed for רב's teaching about an אשם that was sent to graze and then slaughtered as an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's true. The פסוק comes for רב's teaching. רב הונא said in the name of רב: An אשם that was sent off to graze, and someone slaughtered it as an עולה, is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is not needed for the תמורה. It is needed for a different rule, which רב taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא admits the question is right: the תמורת אשם is already known from the הלכה. But ״הוּא״ teaches something new, connected to רב's ruling. רב says that after an אשם is officially sent to graze, if someone went ahead and slaughtered it as an עולה (instead of selling it and using the money for עולות), the עולה is valid after the fact. The next step shows that ״הוּא״ teaches the flip side: before it is sent to graze, slaughtering it as an עולה does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: "So too" — yes, you are right
Was sent off to graze — officially removed from being offered as an אשם
Burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: רב does not say an אשם may be offered as an עולה from the start. His ruling is only about an אשם that was already sent off to graze.

phrases.english: So too, that is correct,
and when the verse comes — it is for Rav's teaching.
As Rav Huna said that Rav said:
a guilt-offering that was sent off to graze,
phrases.notes: It was ruled that it can't be offered as an אשם, so it grazes until it gets a blemish and is sold.

phrases.english: and one slaughtered it for the sake of a burnt-offering
— it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי, וְכִי אֲתָא קְרָא לִדְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by giving the פסוק a different job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agrees with the question and moves the פסוק to a new teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״הוּא״ was needed to keep the תמורת אשם from being offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: That is known from the הלכה; ״הוּא״ is needed for the rule behind רב's ruling.

steps.title: How רב's ruling comes from the word 'It'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב's ruling suggests an אשם not yet sent to graze cannot be offered as an עולה, and that this comes from ״הוּא״ — it stays as it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason it is valid is that it was sent off to graze. But if it was not sent off, it is not valid. For the פסוק says "It": it stays in its present state.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from רב's words. Then it shows that this inference is exactly what the word ״הוּא״ teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ruling depends on the animal having been sent to graze. So before that, an אשם slaughtered as an עולה is not valid. That comes from ״הוּא״: while it is still an אשם it must stay an אשם, and offering it as something else does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: "The reason is because..." — used to draw an inference
"But if not" — the opposite case

steps.whatToRemember: The word ״הוּא״ is not needed for the תמורת אשם, which we know from the הלכה. It teaches that an אשם still waiting to be offered as an אשם is not valid if offered as a different קרבן. Once it is sent to graze, רב says it can be a valid עולה.

phrases.english: The reason it is valid is that it was sent off to graze,
but if it was not sent off — it is not valid.
For the verse says: "It"
— it shall be in its present state.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּנִיתַּק, הָא לֹא נִיתַּק לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from Step 9 by linking רב's ruling to the word ״הוּא״.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Inference from רב's ruling tied back to the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: An אשם not yet sent to graze, slaughtered as an עולה, is not valid, because of ״הוּא״.

steps.title: Back to the rule about a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבי יוחנן's earlier statement that a certain rule is a הלכה about a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: It is a הלכה about a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to an earlier statement of רבי יוחנן. It is setting up a question about it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יוחנן said that the rule about a נזיר's money set aside without saying which קרבן it is for, which goes to voluntary offerings, is a הלכה for a נזיר. The words "about a נזיר" make it sound like this happens only with a נזיר. The next step questions that.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow to avoid wine, haircuts, and טומאת מת
Here: a tradition handed down from משה

phrases.english: The Master said: It is a halakha with regard to a nazirite.
phrases.notes: "The Master" here is רבי יוחנן, quoted earlier on the דף about a נזיר's money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אשם discussion and goes back to an earlier statement about a נזיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן called the rule about a נזיר's money a הלכה about a נזיר.

steps.title: Isn't there another case besides a נזיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the rule really applies only to a נזיר, and starts to quote a ברייתא about other people who bring pairs of birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there no other case? But a ברייתא teaches: And the rest of those in the Torah who must bring pairs of birds...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that this rule is only for a נזיר. It begins to quote a ברייתא that seems to give the same rule for other people; the quote continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן says the rule is about a נזיר, it sounds like no one else has it. The ברייתא talks about other people who must bring a pair of birds, like a poor מצורע. It seems to apply the same rule to them, which would be a problem for רבי יוחנן's wording.

keyTerms.meaning: "And is there no more?" — is this really the only case?
Pairs of birds brought as קרבנות, often by a poor person

phrases.english: And is there no other case? But isn't it taught in a baraita:
and the rest of those in the Torah who must bring pairs of birds,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording quoted in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's wording that the rule is a הלכה about a נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא seems to give the same rule for others who bring pairs of birds, so it is not only for a נזיר.
